minutes.headline: Select Board advised the building committee to fold PACK studio space into phases one and two, and kept comparable-communities list with Gardner added back.
minutes.summary: After a joint executive session with Conservation on litigation, the board jointly appointed a library trustee, heard the Municipal Building Design Committee's schematic update, and heard PACK's space-needs presentation. The board advised the committee to incorporate PACK into phases one and two and to consider 30 School Street. It also settled interview logistics for town manager finalists, took no action on 56 Car, and accepted the comparable communities list with Gardner restored.

what_happened.line: The Select Board advised the building committee to fold PACK studio space into phases one and two of the municipal building project and to consider 30 School Street.
The board voted unanimously to accept the comparable communities list as modified, with Gardner added back.
After a joint executive session on litigation, the board jointly appointed a library trustee by roll call for the remainder of a term ending May 2025.
The board agreed that town manager finalist interviews will be held at the library, with redacted resumes and cover letters attached to the agenda.
The board took no action on the 56 Car property while counsel explores whether deed restrictions can be applied.

why_it_matters: Where PACK is housed affects the cost of the new municipal building, and the minutes record the chair saying total cost could rise beyond the original budget, so residents may later be asked to fund more than first presented.
PACK runs on cable franchise fees that are declining and cover operations but not capital, so a standalone building or a major equipment failure would have to be paid for from other sources.
The comparable communities list is the yardstick for salary and budget comparisons, including the town manager search, so which towns are on it shapes later pay and spending arguments.
